gap: No result ChatGPT got states that RTINGS's 47.6 dBA for the NuPhy Air75 V3 (Blush Nano) is the only named typing-noise figure published for any of the candidates: RTINGS tested its Lofree Flow 2 with Pulse tactile switches rather than the Void silent ones ChatGPT recommends, and no named reviewer I opened gives a dB figure for the Void, Gamakay's Phoenix V3 silent, the Cherry KC 200 MX Silent Red, the Rainy 75 Silent or the Kensington QuietType Pro.
standout_why: Compared against the four cited pages. RTINGS best/quiet already carries the 47.6 dBA figure and its dBA scale. RTINGS best/work already says the Flow 2 was tested with Pulse and gives no dBA. mkbguide quotes about 50 dBA for the Razer Pro Type Ultra and about 47 dBA for an unnamed low-profile board without naming the measurer, and declines to rank by dB. keyboardranker says its keyboards 'were not tested or measured for sound'. No rival sets out side by side which candidates have a named measurement and which do not, or that RTINGS has no figure for the Void, but each piece sits on a cited RTINGS page. The other ten results were not opened.
decides: It confirms the NuPhy Air75 V3 with Blush Nano as the pick on measured noise: it is the only candidate with a public, named figure. It does not let the page rank the Lofree Flow 2 Void or any Gamakay Phoenix V3 silent board on noise; they can be listed only as silent-switch boards, with their quietness attributed to named reviewers' descriptions (PCWorld for the Void per a search result I did not open, Smartzone for the Phoenix V3 silent). The page should say that RTINGS's Flow 2 noise result is for the tactile Pulse unit, and that 47.6 dBA sits between RTINGS's own 45 dBA 'quiet' and 50 dBA 'too loud' marks.

findings.label: Typing noise, RTINGS, Gateron 3.0 Blush Nano silent switches
findings.source_title: The 6 Best Quiet Keyboards - Black Friday 2026 - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS: 'We measured only 47.6 dBA while typing, which is very quiet and likely won't bother people around you.' Its pick for Best Quiet Mechanical Keyboard; added as top pick 2026-04-17, page last updated 2026-10-26. The RTINGS page body is script-rendered, so I read it through the r.jina.ai text rendering of this URL. ChatGPT's answer already quotes this figure.

findings.label: RTINGS scale for typing-noise figures
findings.value: 50 dBA too loud for a quiet keyboard; 45 dBA quiet; 40 dBA or lower very quiet; about 10 dBA sounds roughly twice as loud
findings.source_title: The 6 Best Quiet Keyboards - Black Friday 2026 - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Quoted: 'we expect most people will feel that 50 dBA is too loud for a quiet keyboard' and 'a difference of about 10 dBA will generally sound roughly twice as loud to most listeners'. The 45 and 40 dBA marks came through as a summary of the page, not a verbatim quote; re-read before printing. On this scale the Air75 V3's 47.6 dBA falls between 'quiet' and 'too loud'. Read through the r.jina.ai text rendering.

findings.product: Gamakay TK75 V2 (mechanical, Phoenix V2 silent linear; not a board we list)
findings.label: Notebookcheck on noise, weight and battery (Julian van der Merwe, published 2025-01-18, modified 2026-10-05)

findings.label: Smartzone on noise with Phoenix Silent V3 switches (Max Drechsel, 2026-08-15)
findings.value: No dB figure; 'deutlich leiser als eine herkömmliche Bürotastatur mit Rubberdome-Schaltern' (clearly quieter than a conventional rubber-dome office keyboard); 1,100 g
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75 TMR Test: Ultraleise 75%-Tastatur für Büro & Gaming - Smartzone

findings.label: Measured latency, HLPlanet (Marcus Richardson, 2026-05-18), OSLTT
findings.note: Measured with the Open Source Latency Testing Tool on a unit with Mercury V3 (non-silent) switches. No dB figure. HLPlanet describes the Phoenix V3 Silent, which it did not test in this review, as 'the kind of silent where background noise is louder than the keys'. Latency is secondary for an office question.

findings.label: What the cited non-RTINGS rival pages measure
findings.value: mkbguide: about 50 dBA for the Razer Pro Type Ultra and about 47 dBA for an unnamed older low-profile board, measurer not named, and it declines to rank by dB. keyboardranker: no measurements
findings.source_title: Best Quiet Mechanical Keyboards for the Office (2026) - MKB Guide
findings.note: mkbguide: 'published decibel readings from different sources cannot be ranked against each other'. keyboardranker (https://keyboardranker.com/posts/best-keyboards-for-office-and-quiet/, read 2026-11-21): 'The keyboards were not tested or measured for sound.' mkbguide's picks include the Air75 V3 Blush Nano, Cherry KC 200 MX Silent Red, Lofree Flow 2 84 Void and Logitech MX Mechanical; neither page mentions Gamakay.
